modules.module_title: Prepare Test Environment according to SOPs

pcs.pc_description: review SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) for specific test requirements.
identify and gather all necessary materials and tools listed in the SOPs for wafer testing
verify the functionality and proper calibration of any required measuring tools.
consult equipment recommendations or SOPs for the ideal temperature and humidity range for optimal test performance
utilize thermometers and hygrometers to monitor the test environment conditions
adjust environmental controls (e.g., air conditioning, dehumidifiers) as needed to maintain the specified temperature and humidity levels.
verify that essential utilities like compressed air and power supply are available and functioning properly
conduct a visual inspection of utility lines and connections for any signs of damage or leaks
test the functionality of compressed air pressure and power supply voltage according to established procedures
document the test environment conditions (temperature, humidity, etc.) and any adjustments made according to SOPs

modules.module_title: Set up & Calibrate Wafer Test Equipment

pcs.pc_description: analyze the type of telecom wafers to be tested
review test program requirements for specific functionalities to be evaluated
identify the appropriate test equipment model from available options based on wafer type & test needs and consult SOPs for the selected test equipment model
identify and gather required test accessories like test heads and probes suitable for wafer testing

install the accessories onto the designated ports or fixtures on the test equipment, following established procedures, ensuring proper connection and secure positioning of the test heads and probes for optimal test performance
configure relevant equipment parameters (e.g., voltage levels, signal frequencies), based on the specific test program
ensure parameter settings align with the requirements outlined in the test program for accurate testing of functionalities (e.g., communication channel bandwidth, data integrity)
conduct a visual inspection of the test heads and probes to ensure proper alignment and positioning for contacting the designated test points on the wafers
utilize calibration tools or procedures outlined in SOPs to verify the calibration of test heads and probes
perform necessary adjustments or report the issue for maintenance personnel to address the issue, if calibration is out of specification
initiate a system check function on the test equipment as per SOPs
verify that all components of the test equipment, including accessories, are functioning properly as a system before proceeding with actual testing
identify the relevant test parameters requiring calibration for the wafer test
perform calibration routines for each identified parameter according to established procedures
document calibration results, including dates, performed adjustments, and reference standards used, for traceability purposes

modules.module_title: Load Wafers into the Test Equipment Following Handling Protocols

pcs.pc_description: review SOPs for specific handling procedures for the type of wafer being tested
visually inspect the wafers for any physical damage or defects that might affect testing
clearly label the wafers with identification information according to established protocols for traceability throughout the testing process
select and utilize appropriate handling tools (e.g., vacuum tweezers, transport carriers) designed for safe handling of delicate wafers
refer to SOPs or the test equipment manual for the designated loading pattern specific to the type of wafer being tested
verify that all wafers are loaded according to the pattern to optimize testing efficiency and avoid potential issues during the testing process
double-check the orientation of each loaded wafer to ensure it aligns with the test head and probe configuration for proper contact with the test points
verify that all wafers are securely positioned within the carrier or fixture to prevent any movement or misalignment during testing
secure the wafer carrier or fixture within the test equipment using the designated locking mechanisms
implement established electrostatic discharge (ESD) control procedures throughout the wafer handling process
utilize ESD-safe tools (e.g, grounded tweezers), wear ESD wrist straps grounded to the equipment, and maintain a clean and ESD-safe work environment

modules.module_title: Perform Routine Cleaning and Preventive Maintenance of Equipment

pcs.pc_description: follow established SOPs (Standard Operating Procedures) for cleaning various components of the wafer test equipment
identify and utilize appropriate cleaning materials and equipment for specific components
perform cleaning tasks to ensure a dust-free and contamination-free environment within the test equipment, minimizing potential issues like test signal degradation or device damage
ensure cleaning of areas crucial for proper test execution (e.g., test fixtures, probe tips, wafer contact surfaces)

identify and perform routine maintenance activities on the test equipment according to established schedules (eg. lubricating moving parts, replacing air filters, and calibrating specific test instruments to ensure optimal performance)
maintain a log of completed preventive maintenance activities for each piece of equipment, including dates and details of actions performed
visually inspect the equipment for any signs of wear or damage during cleaning and maintenance procedures, reporting any concerns to appropriate personnel
organize and maintain a clean and clutter-free workspace around the test equipment to prevent accidental damage or contamination of wafers and test components
properly dispose of used cleaning materials and waste generated during maintenance activities in designated bins or containers
keep tools and equipment used for cleaning and maintenance organized and readily accessible for efficient use
report any spills or contamination incidents within the work area promptly for proper cleaning and containment
recognize potential dangers and indications of equipment failure during operation, such as unusual noises, error messages, or unexpected behavior in test results
utilize equipment manuals, troubleshooting guides, and diagnostic tools (e.g., built-in self-test functions) to identify the source of potential failures
observe and document specific details about the malfunction, including error messages displayed, test interruptions, or abnormal equipment behavior
consult with experienced personnel (e.g., engineers, maintenance technicians) for further diagnosis and guidance, when encountering unfamiliar issues
perform basic troubleshooting steps as per established procedures or manufacturer recommendations, such as restarting the equipment, checking cable connections, or resetting specific settings
document the troubleshooting steps taken and their outcomes for future reference and to inform further repair efforts
clearly identify the problem and its impact on test operations (e.g., complete test stoppage, partial functionality loss), if basic troubleshooting fails to resolve the issue
report equipment malfunctions requiring repair work beyond basic troubleshooting capabilities to designated personnel (e.g., maintenance technicians) following established company protocols
record all maintenance activities performed on the test equipment in a detailed and comprehensive manner, including cleaning, preventive maintenance, and repairs

utilize designated logbooks or a computerized maintenance management system to document maintenance activities, including the date, type of maintenance performed, specific actions taken, replacement parts used (if applicable), and any observations made
adhere to company policies for organizing and storing maintenance logs and records electronically or in designated physical binders for future reference and traceability purposes
